headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 5 studies yielded an effect size of 1.05 (95% CI: 0.99–1.12), indicating no statistically significant association between omega-6 fatty acids and prostate cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential positive relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 84.26%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
